## 2026-09-20 — Award-family/current-source evidence sweep

### GSA/open-gsa-redesign — SAM.gov Contract Awards API — STRONG / MASTER REFERRAL — 29/30
- URL: https://github.com/GSA/open-gsa-redesign
- Exact revision: `494b1312e9c6436474840befe6e1964da15932b3`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-20
- Category: Official Schema/API / Dataset Infrastructure / Reusable Component
- Concrete capability: Official machine-readable documentation for SAM.gov's Contract Awards API. It exposes revealed Award/IDV contract records, `solicitationID`, PIID and referenced-IDV identifiers, document versions, obligation/value/date/agency/awardee fields, plus `piidAggregation` that summarizes an award family across base records and modifications and, for IDVs/FSS vehicles, referencing orders/BPAs/calls. `publicDeltaDate` supports last-modified/reveal-date retrieval; `deletedStatus=yes` exposes contracts deleted in the prior six months.
- Rare / undernoticed value: This supplies a first-party award-family and modification lineage layer rather than forcing CaptureBrief to infer incumbent history from flattened spend rows. Public-data semantics also encode an important negative-evidence boundary: DoD records funded/awarded by DoD with Date Signed less than 90 days old are unrevealed to ordinary public users, so absence during that window is not evidence of no award.
- Buyer / painful problem: GovCon capture teams and consultants need defensible incumbent/vehicle/modification history tied to the exact solicitation and legal awardee, not name-based approximations or stale spend dashboards.
- Monetization / first paid wedge: Premium CaptureBrief award/incumbent evidence packet: solicitation -> PIID/IDV family -> base/modification/deletion/delta history -> obligations -> awardee UEI/CAGE/parent identity, with explicit public-reveal and completeness state.
- Build-time / data advantage: Very high. It removes months of contract-family field discovery and supplies authoritative API semantics that are hard to reconstruct from secondary wrappers.
- Evidence inspected: `_apidocs/contract-awards.md` at the exact revision, including revealed/unrevealed definitions, award/IDV types, sync/extract result ceilings, PIID aggregation, deleted-contract behavior, solicitation/PIID filters and account/rate-limit requirements; repository license. The public docs state synchronous search is capped at the first 400,000 records and extracts at 1,000,000, so broad pulls must be partitioned or marked incomplete.
- Public license / rights: `GSA/open-gsa-redesign` is U.S.-government work placed in the U.S. public domain and dedicated worldwide under CC0. SAM.gov account/API/rate-limit and nonpublic-data permissions remain separate.
- Score: A5 + B5 + C5 + D5 + E5 + F4 = **29/30**. F is capped because public DoD reveal lag, result ceilings and authenticated access have to be modeled explicitly.
- Combination opportunities: Curatore/versioned forecasts -> complete SAM solicitation/amendment packet -> `solicitationID` -> Contract Awards PIID/IDV family -> Federal Hierarchy + SAM Entity/Exclusions -> `Nonprofit-Open-Data-Collective/usaspend` transaction/deobligation normalization -> CaptureBrief incumbent conclusion.
- Strongest objection: It is still an API surface with access/rate/result constraints; it does not by itself guarantee complete history unless the collector partitions, records coverage and handles reveal/deletion semantics correctly.
- Next action: Run a 100-award benchmark across civilian and DoD awards and require the same base/mod/IDV/awardee lineage as USAspending-derived history, while forcing `reveal_pending` or `partition_required` instead of false "no award" conclusions.

### govconapi/govconapi-mcp — WATCH — 23/30
- URL: https://github.com/govconapi/govconapi-mcp
- Exact revision: `d8a4ba46b057b885cd8df2f8974775653db15949`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-20
- Category: Repository / External Data Product Comparator
- Concrete capability: MIT MCP client exposing 53 tools over a hosted federal procurement intelligence API spanning SAM opportunities/entities/exclusions, FPDS-style contract transactions, FFATA subawards, SBA DSBS, GSA CALC and GAO protest data, joined on UEI/CAGE/PIID/NAICS. The public product also claims full-text solicitation-attachment indexing including OCR and nested archives.
- Rare / undernoticed value: Strong evidence that buyers will pay for cross-source identifier joins and attachment-level search, and a useful optional provider/comparator for CaptureBrief.
- Buyer / painful problem: GovCon analysts repeatedly rebuild cross-source joins and cannot search requirements buried inside attachments.
- Monetization / first paid wedge: External-provider-assisted CaptureBrief research or a benchmark comparator for attachment/award/entity retrieval.
- Build-time / data advantage: Medium for the public repository because the valuable ingestion/indexing corpus is hosted and not present in the repo; high only if using the external commercial API under its own terms.
- Evidence inspected: README at the exact revision; recursive tree showing MCP core and tool modules but not the underlying ingestion/indexing engine or test corpus; recent history correcting overstated corpus counts and dating coverage snapshots; MIT LICENSE.
- Public license / rights: MIT for repository code. Hosted API, corpus, pricing, usage logs and source-data rights are separate.
- Score: A5 + B5 + C3 + D4 + E3 + F3 = **23/30**.
- Combination opportunities: Use as a benchmark/optional source against official SAM/USAspending evidence, never as the sole system of record.
- Next action: Compare 25 CaptureBrief packets against official sources and GovCon API; quantify attachment recall and identifier-join error before relying on it operationally.

### silent-northwest/govprocure-pp-cli — WATCH — 20/30
- URL: https://github.com/silent-northwest/govprocure-pp-cli
- Exact revision: `ef229e5f83d4a29de7e4dcd7a979d92f18b2b61c`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-20
- Category: Repository / Local Data Workflow
- Concrete capability: Go CLI/MCP that mirrors Grants.gov, SAM.gov opportunities and USAspending awards into local SQLite/FTS5 with typed exit codes, source health, compound search and stale/profile workflows.
- Rare / undernoticed value: Recent commits explicitly removed arbitrary sync limits because fixed ceilings silently excluded valid opportunities, removed a hidden hard-coded search fallback, moved the SAM key out of query strings, and normalized source dates before SQLite comparisons. Those fixes encode useful evidence-grade failure lessons.
- Buyer / painful problem: Small capture/research teams want fast local/offline procurement search without rebuilding three API clients.
- Monetization / first paid wedge: Local analyst toolkit or evidence-gathering sidecar, not a standalone moat.
- Build-time / data advantage: Moderate; working adapters/local schema help, but no repository test suite was found and existing MASTER leaders are deeper.
- Evidence inspected: commit history through the exact revision, recursive tree, README command/data-freshness model, and code-search for tests (none surfaced).
- Public license / rights: README labels the project MIT and links `LICENSE`, but that file is absent at the exact revision. Treat published rights metadata as internally inconsistent; user's separate permission is the working assumption for repository-owned material. Upstream APIs retain their own terms.
- Score: A4 + B3 + C4 + D2 + E3 + F4 = **20/30**.
- Negative knowledge: Never let a fixed sync/search cap or hidden fallback filter produce an apparently complete opportunity universe.
- Next action: Retain as a workflow/reference source; do not elevate unless a tested completeness/provenance layer appears.

### GSA/srt-api — REJECT / DEPRIORITIZE — 14/30
- URL: https://github.com/GSA/srt-api
- Exact revision: `7f529d53055492ab7470585d9bbd92ddfbd1e581`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-20
- What it contains: Older Express/Postgres backend for GSA's Solicitation Review Tool, which ingested SAM solicitations and supported Section 508 compliance predictions/feedback.
- Why rejected: Historical architecture is interesting, but it is stale relative to current SAM/FAR authority and requires privileged environments. No current evidence showed a stronger reusable compliance engine than existing lane leaders. A historical commit message indicated credentials had once been removed; no sensitive values/history were inspected or preserved.
- Public license / rights: No current license was verified at the inspected revision. User's separate permission applies only to repository-owned public material.
- Score: A1 + B2 + C3 + D3 + E2 + F3 = **14/30**.
- Next action: Do not revisit absent a current successor or authoritative Section-508 rule engine.
